about: Londolozi lion prides, coalitions and individuals reconstructed from blog.londolozi.com Lions-category posts (2014-2026). Only what posts state; confidence marks stated vs inferred. Posts conflict in places - see open_questions.

prides.name: Castleton Pride
prides.note: Natal pride of the two founders of the Tsalala Pride (1998). Its own origin is not given.
prides.status: Natal pride of the Tsalala founders (1998); one Tsalala-born female ("Queen") joined it later.
prides.origin: Parent pride of the two females that broke away in 1998 to form the Tsalala Pride.

history.event: Two Castleton females break away to found the Tsalala Pride.

prides.notes: The Tsalala breaking away from Castleton is also noted in 2016-09-03. first_mentioned/last_mentioned = first and last post in the 307-file corpus matching the group name (not the group's active period).

prides.name: Tsalala Pride
prides.note: Two Castleton females break away and den seven cubs ('Two and Seven').
prides.status: Effectively a single lioness (Tsalala Female, b. 2019), alive at last mention (Feb 2026); no surviving cubs since 2019. About 11 lions in 2009 and 10 in 2011; down to one female by June 2018.
prides.origin: Formed in 1998 by two Castleton Pride females (believed pregnant by the West Street Males) who broke away and denned seven cubs near Taylor's Crossing. Named for Tsalala (Gardenia) Pan. Only one cub (the Original Tailless Female) outlived the founders; her descendants are the Tsalala lineage (Legacy post).
aliases: Tsalala core pride (as opposed to the Tsalala Breakaway prides)

history.event: Two females break away from the Castleton Pride and den seven cubs ("Two and Seven").

Attrition to "One and Two": cubs killed by Sparta Pride, hyenas, injury, poaching; one founder kicked by a zebra; remaining founder killed by hyenas Dec 2002 leaving the Original Tailless Female alone.
Original Tailless Female gives birth to twin daughters (the Tsalala Sisters) at Ximpalapala Koppie.
Original Tailless Female loses her tail to hyenas at a zebra kill.
Mapogo Males (six) take over, kill the Rocky Male and all but two of the Sisters' 2006 cubs.
Pride thrives under two Mapogo males (Kinky-tail, Satan); litters in 2008 and 2009 bring it to 11.
Majingilane Males arrive, kill several cubs; the two Sisters join them; the Original Tailless Female leaves with four 2009-born sub-adult females (first Tsalala Breakaway Pride).
Breakaway rejoins briefly; reunion with the Sisters fails; Original Tailless Female returns to natal pride in Nov 2011.
Younger Sister loses her tail to hyenas; eight 2011 cubs reduced to one by May 2012.
Four sub-adult females form the independent Mhangeni Pride.
Original Tailless Female killed by the Mhangeni lionesses; Tailed Sister bears the 2013 litter (3 M, 1 F).
Matimba Males arrive; pride splits; Tailless Sister takes four sub-adults away (second Tsalala Breakaway Pride).
Matimba-sired litters: 2 cubs (Tailed Sister) and 3 cubs (2011 Female).
Core pride and breakaway pride feed together (11 lions) - temporary reunion.
2011 Female and cubs lost; Tailed Sister joins the Tailless Sister in the breakaway.
Tailed Sister found dead.
Tailless Sister dies at Marthly Pools; the 2013-born female is the sole Tsalala lioness.
First litter of the 2013-born female (3 cubs; father a Birmingham male); cubs reduced to one by Aug 2019.
The 2013-born female is killed in the western Sabi Sand; her daughter (b. 2019) is left alone.
Daughter pairs with a Mhangeni lioness for ~2 months.
Daughter's first litter (3 cubs, Plains Camp-sired) is lost.
Second litter lost within a week.

prides.notes: The matriline: Original Tailless Female (b.1998) -> Tsalala Sisters (b.2002; Tailless & Tailed) -> Tsalala 2011 Female / Tsalala 2013 Female (+3 brothers) -> Tsalala Female b.2019 (cubs 2024, 2025). The blog repeatedly stresses that single mothers raising a single cub recurs across generations (Original Tailless 2002; 2013 female 2019). first_mentioned/last_mentioned = first and last post in the 307-file corpus matching the group name (not the group's active period).

prides.name: Tsalala Breakaway Pride (2009–2012)
prides.note: The Original Tailless Female leaves with four 2009-born sub-adults to escape the Majingilane.
prides.origin: In 2010 the Original Tailless Female left the Tsalala Pride with the surviving 2009-born female sub-adults of her daughters (4 young lionesses) to escape the Majingilane; raised them to independence in the north-west Sabi Sand; they then formed the Mhangeni Pride.
aliases: "Breakaway pride" of the Original Tailless Female

history.event: Breakaway formed (Original Tailless Female + 4 female sub-adults).
Attempted reunion with the Tsalala Sisters - sub-adults rebuffed; the Original Tailless Female returns to natal pride a month later.
Sub-adults lose contact with the Original Tailless Female after a flood and form the Mhangeni Pride.

prides.notes: The Epic post (2017-05-01) suspects the cubs she saved were her daughters' (i.e. her granddaughters). first_mentioned/last_mentioned = first and last post in the 307-file corpus matching the group name (not the group's active period).

prides.name: Mhangeni Pride
prides.note: The four sub-adults lose contact with the Original Tailless Female after the Jan 2012 flood and form the Mhangeni Pride.
prides.status: Active (west of Londolozi, rarely seen on the property by 2024-26). Feb 2026: three adult lionesses (two born 2016 sired by Majingilane; one born 2018 sired by Birmingham) plus three Plains-Camp-sired subadults and four cubs born Nov 2025. Jul 2026: one experienced lioness with three ~2.5-year-old subadults seen hunting wildebeest.
prides.origin: Breakaway from the Tsalala Pride at the Majingilane takeover (2010). Founded by four young lionesses born 2009 (one post says 2008) to the Tsalala Sisters and sired by the Mapogo Males; when the Majingilane killed several Tsalala cubs the Original Tailless Female (their grandmother) led the surviving four sub-adults north and raised them to independence (c.18 months); on her return in Oct 2011 the Tsalala Sisters rejected them and the four became a separate pride, named Mhangeni (c.2012-13). Dates of formation vary between posts (2010, Jan 2012, 2013).
aliases: Mhangeni Breakaway (original form, 2010-2013; Tsalala Breakaway sub-adults)

history.event: Pride described as originating from a breakaway of the Tsalala Pride six years earlier (2010) when the Majingilane arrived.
Four 2009-born sub-adult females lose connection with Original Tailless Female in Jan 2012 after the flood and form the Mhangeni Pride; the Original Tailless Female rejoins Tsalala.
2013: Original Tailless Female (aged ~15) is mauled by the Mhangeni females at a zebra carcass and found dead at Marthly Pools (2018-05-20 post says only 'suspected').
First Mhangeni litter (2013): 9 cubs raised to independence under Majingilane protection (a tenth cub disappeared early).
Sept 2015: a clash with rival lions in the north splits the 13-strong pride (4 adult females, 9 sub-adults); a young Sparta male later joins them (14 counted 12 Sep 2015).
Aug 2016: the nine sub-adults (the 'Mhangeni breakaways') briefly rejoin the four mothers, a 'super pride' of 22.

29 Apr 2017: Mhangeni Breakaway Pride (six sister lionesses) permanently split from the Mhangeni females and renamed the Ntsevu Pride; the three brothers had left a few months earlier (Dec 2016 post).
Nov 2017: pride still large (13 lions drinking + 3 females + a Majingilane male = 17 counted).
2018: second batch of 12 sub-adults (9M/3F) pushed out end of 2017, some died; pride reduced to 3 adult lionesses + 1 sub-adult; new litter of 4 cubs mid-2018.
Dec 2019: Othawa Male joins the Mhangeni pride and becomes its protector.
2021: Othawa Male dies; pride left without a male; Plains Camp Males move into the western territory.

2022: one original (2009-born) Mhangeni lioness breaks away to mate with Plains Camp Males, loses the pride and temporarily pairs with the lone Tsalala Female (~Aug-Sep 2022); rejoins pride by Nov 2022 apparently pregnant.
2023: Plains Camp Males dominant over Mhangeni and Ximungwe Prides and siring nine cubs with the Mhangeni.
Jun 2024: pride = 5 lionesses + 10 cubs under Plains Camp Males; two original lionesses (b.2009, aged 15) still alive, one toothless.
2024: Mhangeni pride presumed to have killed the two Nkuhuma Breakaway lionesses (Ridge Nose and Amber Eyes).
2025-26: Plains Camp Males move north; Nkumati Coalition (Nkuhuma + Talamati males) takes over mating rights; one 2018-born lioness has 4 cubs (Nov 2025).

prides.notes: Contradictions: (1) founders' birth year 2009 (most posts) vs 2008 ('eleven years old' in 2019-12-02). (2) Fathers: first cubs of the original four were Mapogo-sired; later litters Majingilane (2013, 2015/16), Birmingham (2018), Othawa (2020-21), Plains Camp (2023), Nkumati (2025). (3) The 2013 litter 'split to form Ntsevu in 2015' (2024-06-10) vs renamed April 2017 (2017-04-29). (4) 2024-06-10 lists five lionesses incl. two born 2009, but 2026-02-12 lists only three adults (b.2016 x2, b.2018) - fate of the two originals not stated. (5) 2022-08-10 composition: two older original lionesses, two from the 2015/16 litter of 12, one from the 2018 litter, one 2021 Othawa cub.

prides.name: Tsalala Breakaway Pride (2015–2018)
prides.note: The younger Tailless Sister takes four 2013-born sub-adults away from the incoming Matimba Males; ends when she dies (June 2018).
prides.status: Extinct as a separate group by June 2018 (Tailless Sister died; 2013 female alone).
prides.origin: Formed Sept 2015 when the younger Tailless Sister took the four 2013-born sub-adults (3 males, 1 female) of her sister away from the incoming Matimba Males; wandered widely (Manyalethi, Kruger) for a year and returned in late 2016; denned a litter in March 2017.

history.event: Breakaway pride formed.
Tailless female and three sub-adults seen on Londolozi; one male missing, one injured.
Pride of 5 (Tailless + 4 sub-adults) hunting buffalo in SW Londolozi.
Three Tsalala young males disperse; breakaway reduced to Tailless female, 2013 female and cubs; reunion with core pride on a waterbuck kill.
Tailed Sister joins the breakaway; young breakaway cub lost.
Tailless Sister dies.

prides.name: Ntsevu Pride
prides.note: Six lionesses of the first Mhangeni litter (2013) split from their mothers; renamed Ntsevu ('six') on 29 Apr 2017.
prides.status: active (post-2024 'Ntsevu' = smaller faction of 3 original lionesses plus Ndzhenga-sired cubs, mostly north of / east of the Sand River; still mating with Gijima Males in 2025-26)
prides.origin: Six lionesses (plus three brothers) of the first Mhangeni litter (born 2013, sired by the Majingilane) who split from their mothers (the Mhangeni Pride) as sub-adults ~2015-16 and were renamed 'Ntsevu' ('six' in Shangaan) on 2017-04-29. Mhangeni -> Tsalala -> Castleton lineage. Mated with Matshipiri, Matimba, Majingilane then settled with the Birmingham Males (2018-2021), then Ndzhenga Males (Nov 2021-Aug 2025), then Gijima Males (from Aug 2025).
aliases: Mhangeni Breakaway Pride / Mhangeni Breakaways (until 29 Apr 2017)
Kambula Pride (the name Mala Mala used for the same pride, per 2024-03-21)

history.event: Mhangeni Breakaway pride formally renamed the Ntsevu Pride; six lionesses no longer rejoining the adult Mhangeni females.
Ntsevu pushed the Sparta pride out of the central/south-east range and killed one Sparta lioness.
Birmingham Males (4) become the Ntsevu's dominant/mating coalition (mating observed for months; first cubs 2018).
Ndzhenga Males (4) arrive in early Nov 2021; the surviving Birmingham Male is pushed out; Ntsevu mothers flee east/north with their 11 cubs, 7 lost.
11-12 sub-adults (6 males, 5-6 females; born mid-2018) leave the pride to become the Ntsevu Breakaway Pride.
Two Ntsevu mothers (the 'Ntsevu Two') reappear with the last 4 Birmingham-sired cubs, having broken away from the main pride after the Ndzhenga arrival.

Pride officially divided in two: smaller faction (3 original lionesses, living in northern Mala Mala) keeps the name Ntsevu; larger faction (1 original + 4/5 Birmingham-sired daughters + Ndzhenga-sired cubs) named Kambula Pride.
After the Gijima Males push north (Aug-Nov 2025), the 3-lioness Ntsevu Pride with 3 cubs follows the Ndzhenga Males north; one Gijima Male mates with a Ntsevu lioness (Aug, Sep, Nov 2025).

prides.notes: Pre-2024 blog posts use 'Ntsevu' for the whole pride (6 founding lionesses + cubs). From 24 Mar 2024 the name is restricted to the smaller faction. Counts of cubs/sub-adults conflict between posts (see open_questions).

prides.name: Ntsevu Breakaway Pride
prides.note: Eleven to twelve sub-adults (born 2018) leave the Ntsevu Pride in Aug 2021; dispersed by 2025.
prides.status: dispersed: 4 males roam as a nomadic coalition (north to Manyelethi/Nkuhuma area and back); lone sister partnered with the Styx Male; 2 older males in Kruger NP
prides.origin: Litter of 12 (6 males, 6 females) born to the Ntsevu lionesses, sired by the Birmingham Males, mid-2018 (plus a June-2019 litter of 4 from which a male and the breakaway female derive). Left the pride in 2021 and were scattered by the Ndzhenga arrival. Four older females rejoined their mothers (-> Kambula daughters); two younger females stayed with the brothers, later one (the 'breakaway female').

history.event: 11 sub-adults leave pride (males transitioning to nomads, females tagging along).
Six young males split into groups of three; Ndzhenga Males' arrival (Nov 2021) forced them southwest; sub-adult females largely rejoin mothers.
Original 12 split: oldest male in Kruger NP, second oldest between Kruger and Sabi Sand, four males + two younger females roam Sabi Sand; four older females rejoined mothers.
Six young males have all left the pride; two went NE into Kruger; the other four plus one 2019-born female roam the south-west.
The four males move north to the Manyelethi reserve and mate with Nkuhuma Pride lionesses.
Lone sister now with the Styx Young Male; brothers in the north.
Largest male injured Nov 2024 (possible run-in with Mantimahle Males) and temporarily separated; all four reunite by 26 Jan 2025.

prides.notes: Blog still calls them the 'Ntsevu Breakaways' in Jan 2025 and 'Kambula Males' in Nov 2024-Jul 2025.

prides.name: Kambula Pride
prides.note: Name adopted on 21 Mar 2024 for the larger faction of the old Ntsevu Pride after the Ndzhenga takeover.
prides.status: active but fractured into three factions (Nov 2025 onward)
prides.origin: Name given by Mala Mala to the Ntsevu Pride; officially adopted by Londolozi on 2024-03-21 for the larger faction of the old Ntsevu Pride after the Ndzhenga takeover: one founding Ntsevu lioness (born 2013) plus four-five daughters born 2018 (Birmingham-sired) and their Ndzhenga-sired cubs (Nov 2022-Aug 2023).
aliases: Ntsevu Pride (pre-2024 name for the same lions)
Kambula Breakaway Pride (the 2025 sub-adult faction + mentor lioness)

history.event: Created as a named pride when the old Ntsevu Pride was divided into 'Ntsevu' (3 originals) and 'Kambula' (1 original + 2018 daughters).
Pride 'at a crossroads': 11 sub-adults (7 males, 4 females) travel with one adult lioness; the other four lionesses raise two new litters (4 cubs + 2 cubs) separately.
Two adult lionesses deliberately isolate with six new cubs (Ndzhenga-sired) away from the sub-adults over ~10 months.

Pride formally described as three factions: (1) eldest lioness + 11 sub-adults heading into the Kruger; (2) two lionesses with 6 Ndzhenga-sired cubs; (3) two lionesses with new Gijima-sired litter(s) in the south-east.
Gijima Males take over the territory; Ndzhenga Males withdraw north; first Gijima-sired litter (4 cubs) discovered; one sub-adult male killed by Gijima Males.
One Kambula female reported to have lost her litter to the dark-maned Gijima Male; second female still nursing.
Two Kambula lionesses (the 'Gijima pair') give birth again in April 2026, denning together on the Sand River.
Kambula Pride and the two Gijima Males seen together with eight cubs.

prides.name: Nkuhuma Pride
prides.note: Originates north of Londolozi; the Talamati Pride broke away from it in 2007.
prides.status: Active, northern Sabi Sand / Marthly / Manyeleti. Fractured into factions (3 in Aug 2022, 23 lions). Mid-2024: four adult females, three sub-adult females, one sub-adult male. 2026: Ndzhenga Males pursuing/siring with the pride in the north (inferred).
prides.origin: Originates north of Londolozi ('Nkuhuma is the Shangaan name for Brown Ivory Tree'). Talamati Pride broke away from it in 2007. Named matriarchs include littermates Ridge Nose and Amber Eyes (born Dec 2012, sired by Matimba Males). Moved onto Marthly (northern Londolozi) as the Tsalala Pride dwindled - first seen there Jan 2020 per 2020-03-05, but 2022-08-10 says 'we began to see them on Marthly in 2018'.

history.event: Jan 2020: 16 lions (6 females, 9 cubs, 1 Northern Avoca male) first seen on Marthly; cubs sired by Northern Avoca Males.
Aug 2020: 8 lionesses + 9 cubs with Avoca males 'often in tow'.
Aug 2022: three factions (23 lions): (1) two Dec-2012 littermates with Plains-Camp cubs, (2) two adults + seven 2019 subadults (5M/2F), (3) three mid-2016 females + seven 2021 subadults (3M/4F).

Two Dec-2012 lionesses (Ridge Nose, Amber Eyes) had broken away west and mated with Plains Camp Males ('Nkuhuma Breakaway Pride'); both later killed, presumably by Mhangeni pride; their two cubs (b.2022) survived.
Jul 2024: Plains Camp Males encroaching on pride after Black Dam Males left and Northern Avoca Male aged.
Sep 2024: Ntsevu Breakaway Males move to Manyeleti and mate with Nkuhuma lionesses.

prides.notes: Several posts use 'Nkuhuma Breakaway' for different things: (a) Mar 2022 'Nkuhuma Breakaway pride' with Avoca males (2022-03-31), (b) the two Dec-2012 lionesses who left to the west, (c) their two surviving offspring, the 'Nkuhuma Breakaways' (young male and female, b.2022). Pride size reported as 16 (Jan 2020), 17 (Aug 2020), 23 (Aug 2022).

prides.name: Talamati Pride
prides.note: Broke away from the Nkuhuma Pride in 2007 when the Mapogo took over from the Manyeleti Males.
prides.status: Active but without fixed territory in 2023; 2023: five lionesses (oldest 'Silver-eye', ~15 yrs in 2022, plus four ~5-year-olds) and two young males who had separated from the pride. Related 'Talamati Breakaway Pride' = Msuthlu Pride (2025).
prides.origin: Broke away from the Nkuhuma Pride in 2007 when the Mapogo took over from the Manyeleti Males; initially the Nkuhuma Breakaway Pride, taken over by the 'Old Nkuhuma Males' who sired two females (incl. the one-eyed 'Silver-eye'); dispersed to Kruger NP in 2008 with those males; named after Talamati Bushveld Camp in 2011; returned to the Sabi Sands in 2011.

history.event: Succession of coalitions: Matimba Males (2011-2015) -> Selati Males (2015) -> Northern Avoca Males (2019); Matimba and Selati daughters later mate with the Imbali Male (2021).
First arrival on Londolozi mid-April 2022: 8 lions (2 adult females + 2 young males + 4 young females; ninth is Dark-maned Northern Avoca male).
Aug 2023: pride has no territory of its own; four young lionesses + oldest lioness; two young males separate.
Oct 2025: 'Msuthlu Pride (formerly the Talamati Breakaway Pride)' is mentioned as returning to Londolozi with the Gijima Males.

prides.notes: first_mentioned 2016-04-02 refers to nomadic Talamati MALES only; pride first seen on Londolozi mid-Apr 2022. Talamati young male sired by Matimba Males seen with Mhangeni breakaways in 2016 (2016-08-20). In July 2022 the pride was described as 'newest pride' even though a 2016 Talamati young male was seen on Londolozi. Msuthlu Pride covered by another agent.

prides.name: Msuthlu Pride
prides.note: Described as 'formerly the Talamati Breakaway Pride'; first met in 2022 in the north of the reserve.
prides.status: active; one of the most-viewed prides on Londolozi 2025-26, now fragmenting (Sep 2026)
prides.origin: Described as 'formerly the Talamati Breakaway Pride' (2025-10-05). First met in 2022 in the north of the reserve (per 2026-04-04) and later settled in the far south of the Sabi Sand under the Gijima Males. Originally 4 adult lionesses and their offspring, 14 lions in total, younger members sired by the Gijima Males.

history.event: Gijima Males named as dominant over the Styx, Southern and Msuthlu prides; pride starts following them north.
Furthest north yet; kill a buffalo with the Gijima Males; Gijima Males named as fathers of the pride's cubs.

With the Ndzhenga and Gijima males swapping territory, Msuthlu become the 'resident pride roaming central Londolozi': 3 adult lionesses, 2 sub-adult males, 2 sub-adult females and 3 younger cubs seen most often.
Adult females come into heat and mate with the N'waswitsaka (Nwaswitshaka) Males in the south; 11 known members.
Pride no longer cohesive; Gijima Males moved north, Nwaswitshaka Males prominent in south; they harass a young Msuthlu male while two adult females defend him.

prides.notes: Exact link to the Talamati Pride (broke from Nkuhuma 2007) is only stated as 'formerly the Talamati Breakaway Pride' in one post; see open_questions.

prides.name: Nkuhuma Breakaway Pride
prides.note: Two Nkuhuma lionesses broke away westward and mated with the Plains Camp Males; both were killed in 2024, leaving two young orphans.
prides.status: Pride of two: a young male and female (born 2022, sired by Plains Camp Males), orphaned after their mothers were killed in early-mid 2024. Roaming nomadically in western/northern Londolozi; male began roaming south-east in mid-2025 and was involved in a fight with the blonde Gijima Male in 2026.
prides.origin: Two adult Nkuhuma lionesses (Ridge Nose and Amber Eyes, born Dec 2012, sired by Matimba Males) broke away westward after the Ndzhenga/Plains Camp arrivals and mated with Plains Camp Males; one raised two cubs (1M, 1F) born 2022.

history.event: Both adult lionesses killed 'presumably by the Mhangeni Pride'; two ~2.5-year-old cubs left to fend for themselves.
Young male ranging further east/south; sister may separate as she nears maturity.
Male (b.2022) confronts and injures the blonde Gijima Male; moving with his sister.

prides.name: Sparta Pride
prides.note: Long-resident Londolozi pride (viewed for over 40 years); down to one female by Nov 2020.
prides.status: Collapsed: one female left by Nov 2020, no longer seen on Londolozi.
prides.origin: Long-resident Londolozi pride (viewed >40 years); 17 lions in 2004 and over 20 at its peak; its lioness line produced the Mapogo (a littermate of the old Sparta lioness). Lost males in 2015 (Sparta Males of 2012 chased out by their Majingilane fathers) and females 2015-2017.

history.event: Old lioness (Mapogo littermate) dies; three females raise 7 cubs under the Majingilane.
The three Sparta Males of 2012 are chased out by the Majingilane.
Pride down to 2 adult females + 1 sub-adult female and (from 2016) 4 Matshipiri-sired cubs.
A Sparta lioness is killed by the six Mhangeni breakaway (Ntsevu) lionesses.

prides.notes: Peripheral; included because the Tsalala Young Male (2005) joined it and the Majingilane/Mapogo lines intersect. first_mentioned/last_mentioned = first and last post in the 307-file corpus matching the group name (not the group's active period).
members: Old Sparta lioness (littermate of the Mapogo)
Two Sparta lionesses born 2007 (cubs of the last Shaw's male)
Sparta lioness killed by the Ntsevu (Mar-Apr 2017)
Sparta cubs of 2016 (sired by the Matshipiri Males)
Sparta young male who joined the Mhangeni (2015)

prides.name: Styx Pride
prides.note: Old pride (14 lions in 2004), later semi-nomadic, then established in the south of Londolozi.
prides.origin: Old pride of 14 lions at Londolozi in 2004 (Shaws Males took over Styx and Sparta prides in 2006). 2018-2020: visited Londolozi's north from the north-east, semi-nomadic by Aug 2020 after losing male cover. Later (2022) described as '3 adults and 11 cubs' established south of Londolozi, covered by the Ndzhenga Males who sired litters with them; by 2025 covered by the Gijima Males.

history.event: Styx pride semi-vagrant, without a dominant male; joined by one Nkuhuma young male.
Styx Pride: 3 adults, 11 cubs; moved south into old Ndzhenga territory, covered by Ndzhenga Males.
Ndzhenga Males had sired several litters with the Styx Pride before moving north.
Now dominated by the Gijima Males (along with Southern and Msuthlu prides).

prides.notes: 'Styx Male' (b. 2021) is a son of the Ndzhenga Males and a Styx-pride litter. Separate from the older 'Styx Males' coalition of 2014-15 and 'Styx Young Male (b.2016)' who broke away with an Nkuhuma young male.
members: Styx Male (young, blonde)
Styx Young Male (b. 2016) - Nkuhuma partner
Styx Pride lionesses (3 adults + 11 cubs, 2022)
Styx Male (born 2016, Styx/Nkuhuma pair)
Styx Male (born 2021, son of an Ndzhenga male)

prides.name: Southern Pride
prides.note: Once the largest pride in the Sabi Sand; nearly extinct by 2021, new offspring in 2025.
prides.status: nearly extinct by 2021 (one adult female + 2 cubs); 2025 new offspring sired by Gijima Males
prides.origin: Once the largest pride in the Sabi Sand (>10 adults), ranging across central-southern Sabi Sands. By April 2021 only one adult female and a wounded sub-adult remained on Londolozi's south; the sub-adult believed to have died soon after; adult female raising two cubs (~6 months old in Apr 2021).

history.event: Pride reduced to a single adult female; reported with 2 cubs.
Gijima Males protecting new offspring within the Southern Pride.
Gijima Males dominant over the Southern Pride.

members: Last adult Southern Pride lioness (April 2021)

prides.name: Othawa Pride
prides.note: Known only as a western pride whose lionesses were mated by the Matimba Males in 2018.
prides.status: unknown; neighbouring western pride (2026: 'neighbouring Othawa and Ximungwe Prides')
prides.origin: Only known as a western pride whose lionesses were mated by the Matimba Males in 2018 and later neighbours of the Mhangeni. The lone 'Othawa Male' shares the geographic name, but the posts do not explicitly say he was born into this pride.

prides.name: Ximungwe Pride
prides.note: Western-sector pride dominated by the Plains Camp Males; renamed Bateleur Pride in Feb 2026.
prides.status: Western-sector pride, dominated by Plains Camp Males (2023-24); described as the 'Ximungwe (now Bateleur) Pride' in Feb 2026 with the Plains Camp Males moving north following it.
prides.origin: Not stated in these posts. Named Ximungwe Pride (also leopard names Ximungwe are unrelated leopards).

history.event: Plains Camp Males described as dominant over Mhangeni and Ximungwe Prides.
Plains Camp Males have sired cubs with the Ximungwe Pride.
Altercation between Tsalala Female and the Ximugwe Pride near her den, Nov 2024.
Renamed Bateleur Pride; Plains Camp Males push north after it, leaving the south-west open to the Nkumati Coalition.

prides.notes: Not otherwise described; no individuals named.

nodes.label: Tsalala founder female 1 (co-founder; kicked by zebra)
aliases: one of the "Two" in the Two and Seven Pride
nodes.birthNote: Adult in 1998; one of two Castleton Pride females who broke away.
nodes.fate: Kicked in the head by a zebra stallion and later died of her injuries (undated, between about 1999 and 2002).
nodes.notes: Legacy post never says which of the two founders was the mother of the Original Tailless Female; the one who survived (founder 2) is inferred to be her mother because she died in Dec 2002 when the Original Tailless was ~4 (Epic post).

nodes.label: Tsalala founder female 2 (mother of the Original Tailless Female)
nodes.birthNote: Adult in 1998; one of two Castleton Pride females who broke away.
nodes.fate: Old and slow; killed by hyenas in front of Tree Camp in December 2002 (Legacy).
nodes.notes: Maternity of the Original Tailless inferred: the Epic post says the Original Tailless was left the only pride member when her mother died when she was 4; Legacy says the pride was reduced to "mother and daughter" before Dec 2002.

nodes.label: The seven cubs of the 1998 Castleton breakaway ("Two and Seven" litter)
nodes.birthNote: Denned in the Sand River near Taylor's Crossing; sired (believed) by the West Street Males.
nodes.fate: Three cubs killed in a clash with the Sparta Pride; a female cub killed by hyenas; a male cub died after his back was broken at a buffalo kill at Maidies Dam; a male was later found poached; one female (the Original Tailless Female) survived.
nodes.notes: Group entry. The 2021-05-04 post gives "four cubs" (one of which survived to be the Original Tailless) denned at Ximpalapala Koppie instead of seven near Taylor's Crossing - see open_questions.

nodes.label: Original Tailless Female
nodes.birthNote: Born 1998 (Epic post); sole surviving cub of the founding breakaway litter (Legacy).
nodes.fate: Mauled by the Mhangeni lionesses (her granddaughters) at a zebra carcass; remains found next day at Marthly Pools, 2013, aged ~15. Legacy states the mauling; 2018 posts say "suspected".
nodes.notes: Mated with the Marthly Males (2002). Lost her tail to hyenas in 2005 after a zebra kill (chewed off the stump), hence the name. Reached the Majingilane takeover (2010) as matriarch; took the surviving 2009 female cubs of her daughters away north and raised them (the future Mhangeni Pride) - the Epic post says these were probably her daughters' cubs, not her own. Rejoined the Tsalala Pride Oct-Nov 2011 and helped it kill a buffalo after the Nov 2011 hyena attack on her daughter. Legacy counts the Aug 2012 cub as her 12th.

nodes.label: Tsalala Sister - the (New) Tailless Female
nodes.pride: Tsalala Pride, then Tsalala Breakaway Pride (2015-2018)
nodes.birthNote: Born December 2002 on Ximpalapala Koppie, twin of the Tailed Female; sired by the Marthly Males (Legacy).
nodes.fate: Found dead ~6 June 2018 at Marthly Pools within metres of where her mother died; had been found badly wounded on 30 May 2018; injuries believed inflicted by Ntsevu lionesses (inference by author).
nodes.notes: Lost her tail to hyenas on 1 Nov 2011 (Legacy; the 2016-05-23 post says 2012). In Sept 2015 took the four 2013-born sub-adults (3 males, 1 female - her sister's litter) away from the Matimba Males, forming the Tsalala Breakaway Pride; rejoined pride briefly Aug 2017; after the Tailed Female's death in Feb 2018 was the last senior Tsalala female. Which Sister bore which 2011 litter is not stated; assignment (Feb 2011 litter = Tailed; May 2011 litter = Tailless) is inferred from the 2016-03-31, 2018-03-22 and Legacy posts. Nov 2016 post says a Matimba male was seen mating with "the tailless Tsalala lioness", contradicting the Epic post that only the two remaining (non-breakaway) females mated with the Matimbas.

nodes.label: Tsalala Sister - the Tailed Female
nodes.birthNote: Born December 2002 on Ximpalapala Koppie, twin of the Tailless Female; sired by the Marthly Males (Legacy).
nodes.fate: Carcass found 19 Feb 2018 just below Ximpalapala crest, aged ~15; had been skeletal and isolated from the pride for weeks and was left behind by her sister and the pride; cause unknown (hyenas or natural causes).
nodes.notes: Mated with the Rocky Male (2006 litter), Mapogo (2009 litter), Majingilane (2011, 2013 litters) and the Matimba Males (2016 litter) in turn. In Sept 2015 she (not the Tailless Female) stayed with the 2011 female while the Tailless Female took the Tsalala sub-adults away. Ximpalapala Koppie is where she denned multiple litters and where her carcass was found.

nodes.label: Tsalala Young Male (b. 2005)
nodes.birthNote: Son of the Original Tailless Female (from her 2005 litter of 2 males + 2 females); survived the hyena incident that cost her her tail.
nodes.fate: Forced to flee the Mapogo (c. 2007-08); joined the Sparta Pride; in 2010 "an impressive specimen" but unable to cement a place without a coalition. 2019 post recalls him on a rhino kill south of Londolozi with Sparta males. Later fate not stated.
nodes.notes: Legacy: "At three years old the other surviving sub-adult male ... had the choice to either stay or flee and flee he did" (so ~2008).

nodes.label: Original Tailless Female's 2005 litter - other cubs (2 females, 1 male)
nodes.birthNote: Litter of four (2 M, 2 F) about six months old when their mother lost her tail in 2005.
nodes.fate: Two female cubs did not survive (Epic: lost to starvation while mother could not hunt); one young male was killed by the Shaw's Males.
nodes.notes: Group entry.

nodes.label: Rocky Male
nodes.pride: Territorial male over the Tsalala Pride (c. 2006)
nodes.birthNote: Unknown.
nodes.fate: Caught, killed and eaten by the Mapogo Males in early 2007 (Legacy: "very unusual behaviour").
nodes.notes: Sire of the Tsalala Sisters' first litters (April 2006).

nodes.label: Tsalala Sisters' first litters (April 2006; six cubs)
nodes.birthNote: Born April 2006 on Ximpalapala Koppie, to the two Tsalala Sisters at age 3.5 (6 cubs total).
nodes.fate: Mapogo Males killed all but two cubs; one female disappeared, was assumed dead, but surfaced in the Castleton Pride (see tsalala-castleton-queen-female-2006).
nodes.notes: Group entry.

nodes.label: Castleton Pride female "Queen" (Tsalala-born, 2006)
nodes.birthNote: One of the Tsalala Sisters' 2006 cubs; thought dead after the Mapogo takeover but joined the Castleton Pride.
nodes.fate: Alive in late 2011 (identified by her reddish eyes); later fate not stated.
nodes.notes: Legacy: "Unbeknown to her they were distant relatives. For five years, Londolozi were unaware of this change in pride until late 2011".

nodes.label: Original Tailless Female's 2008 litter (2 males, 2 females)
nodes.birthNote: Born early 2008 after the Tailless Female separated from the pride.
nodes.fate: Killed by the Majingilane Males in 2010 (Legacy: two killed quickly, two more later; Epic: four Tsalala cubs killed). Identification of the victims as exactly this litter is inferred.
nodes.notes: Group entry. Legacy counts 2 male + 2 female cubs (2008) and 4 female cubs (2009).

nodes.label: Mhangeni Pride original lionesses (four sisters/cousins born 2009)
nodes.birthNote: Four female cubs born 2009, two to each Tsalala Sister, fathered by the Mapogo Males (Kinky-tail and Satan per Legacy).
nodes.fate: Raised from sub-adulthood by the Original Tailless Female; formed the Mhangeni Pride (2012). Two still alive in 2024, aged ~15; one had lost her teeth.
nodes.notes: Group entry. Also called the "Mhangeni breakaway" lionesses in 2012-13. Their own mothers abandoned them for the Majingilane in 2010. 2018-05-30 and Legacy say the Original Tailless died after a mauling by the Mhangeni lionesses ("her granddaughters").

nodes.label: Tsalala 2011 Female
nodes.birthNote: Born early February 2011 (Legacy) - sole survivor of the eight 2011 cubs; sired by the Majingilane Males.
nodes.fate: Last confirmed Sept/Oct 2017; reported missing with a cub after a squabble with other lions (presumed Majingilane); presumed dead. Not seen again; Legacy: "an altercation with some males ... The 2011 Female had gone missing".
nodes.notes: Accepted by the Majingilane Males (her fathers) as she matured. Her 2016 litter was sired by the Matimba Males (Legacy / Epic) though a 2018 post allows Majingilane as possible sire for later cubs. Maternity inferred from "the older tailed female and her daughter from 2011" (2016-03-31).

nodes.label: Tsalala cubs of 2011 (other than the 2011 Female)
nodes.birthNote: Two litters: early Feb 2011 (3 F + 1 M) and 29 May 2011 (3 M + 1 F); sired by the Majingilane Males. Eight cubs in total including the 2011 Female.
nodes.fate: Two May-litter males killed hunting buffalo (autumn 2011); the five-month-old May male (who survived 10 days alone in Nov 2011) was killed 26 Dec 2011 by the Scar-Nose Majingilane male; a Feb-litter male and female swept away in the Jan 2012 flood; two further females gone before May 2012.
nodes.notes: Group entry. The Feb 2011 litter is described as "the second female's"; first Sister's earlier litter failed (probably killed by Majingilane).

nodes.label: Original Tailless Female's single cub (2012)
nodes.birthNote: Born August 2012 (her 12th cub per Legacy); father not stated.
nodes.fate: Disappeared at ~4 months old.
nodes.notes: Photo caption in 2018-02-20 post: "born to her mother, the old Tailless female, but never made it to adulthood".

nodes.label: Tsalala Female (2013 litter) - mother of the 2019 cub
nodes.pride: Tsalala Pride (last adult); Tsalala Breakaway Pride (2015-2018)
nodes.birthNote: Born winter 2013 in a cave on a koppie by the Manyelethi (Southern Cross Koppies); only female of a litter of four (3 M + 1 F). Legacy tables and the 2022-09-19 post say 2014.
nodes.fate: Found dead 20 Nov 2021 in the Sand River in the western Sabi Sand, near full term pregnancy; bite marks on her neck - killed by male lions (Plains Camp Males believed responsible per 2023-12-11).
nodes.notes: All four cubs of her litter reached independence. Went with the Tailless Female (aunt) in the 2015 breakaway; became the sole surviving Tsalala female after June 2018; mated with a Birmingham male (Oct and Dec 2018) and gave birth in March 2019 on the koppie where she herself was born; killed a buffalo alone in July 2019; was attacked by the Ntsevu Pride and a Birmingham male in May 2020 but escaped; mated with the Tumbela Males in Aug 2021.

nodes.label: Tsalala Males (three brothers of the 2013 litter)
nodes.birthNote: Three male cubs of the Tailed Female's 2013 litter, sired by the Majingilane Males.
nodes.fate: Dispersed as a nomadic trio (last seen on Londolozi Aug 2018; 2019 post says they went south, probably into Kruger). Legacy says they were electrocuted in the Kruger National Park feeding on a giraffe touching power lines, dating it after Aug 2017 - conflicts with 2018 sightings.
nodes.notes: Group entry for three unidentified brothers; individual males are not distinguished. Returned briefly May and Aug 2018 (killed a zebra on 2018-08-21).

nodes.label: Tsalala cubs of March 2016 (Tailed Female's litter of 2)
nodes.birthNote: Born March 2016 in the Manyelethi riverbed, sired by the Matimba Males; Legacy says two female cubs.
nodes.fate: All Matimba-sired cubs died by early 2018 (the "5 cubs ... none survived"); several lost Sept-Oct 2017 after a clash with other lions; fate of each not documented.
nodes.notes: Group entry. 2017-10-30 mentions "1 older male" among the youngsters, whereas Legacy lists all five 2016 cubs as females.

nodes.label: Tsalala cubs of June 2016 (2011 Female's litter of 3)
nodes.birthNote: Born ~early June 2016 near Marthly Pools to the 2011 Female (her first litter); Legacy: three female cubs; sire Matimba Males.
nodes.fate: All lost by early 2018; the 2011 Female and a young female cub went missing Oct 2017 and the remaining cubs "never made it".
nodes.notes: Group entry. Combined with the March 2016 litter the pride had five cubs in Oct 2016.

nodes.label: Tsalala Breakaway cubs of 2017 (Tailless Female's litter)
nodes.birthNote: Born March 2017 on Ximpalapala Koppie (3 cubs per Legacy, 2 by April); sire unclear - Matimba or Majingilane.
nodes.fate: One died very young; one lost at ~8 months (Oct 2017, possibly killed by other lions); the last (a male) was emaciated and not expected to live in May 2018 - death not confirmed.
nodes.notes: Group entry. 2018-05-07 states "Only one Tsalala cub is still alive".

nodes.label: Tsalala Female (b. March 2019) - the last Tsalala lioness
nodes.birthNote: Born first week of March 2019 in the cave on Southern Cross Koppies where her mother was born; one of three cubs (1 M + 2 F); father a Birmingham male.
nodes.fate: Alive at last mention (Feb 2026). Mother killed Nov 2021; has since raised no surviving cubs (3 in 2024, lost Oct-Nov 2024; litter of late Sept 2025 lost within a week; possible new den Feb 2026 unconfirmed).
nodes.notes: Escaped an attack by the Ntsevu Pride and a Birmingham male with her mother in May 2020; solitary from Nov 2021; paired with the Mhangeni Lioness (Aug-Sept 2022); mated with the Skorro Young Male (Nov 2023), the Plains Camp Males (Dec 2023-Feb 2024; Jan 2025), the Kruger Male (May 2025) and both Gijima Males (Nov 2025). Denned 2024 on rocks west of Londolozi.

nodes.label: Tsalala cubs of March 2019 - the two siblings of the Tsalala Female
nodes.birthNote: Litter of three born ~first week of March 2019 (1 M + 2 F per Legacy); the Tsalala Female is the survivor.
nodes.fate: Aug 2019: attacked by a (suspected) male leopard; at least one confirmed killed (Legacy: two killed a month after July 2019). The remaining cub was a female.
nodes.notes: Group entry (one male, one female).

nodes.label: Tsalala Female's 2024 cubs (2 females, 1 male)
nodes.birthNote: Born ~May 2024 in a rocky outcrop west of Londolozi (reported with a litter of three from early July 2024); sired (almost certainly) by the Plains Camp Males.
nodes.fate: One female lost late Oct/early Nov 2024 after an encounter with nomads (Kruger Male + Southern Avoca Male); the other two lost days later after an altercation with the Ximungwe Pride; Jan 2025 post suggests the smaller Plains Camp male as possible killer.
nodes.notes: Group entry. The 2024-11-05 post says "one of the female cubs" died first and a female and a male remained.

nodes.label: Tsalala Female's late-September 2025 litter
nodes.birthNote: Second litter, born late Sept 2025 on a koppie on Singita; litter size unknown; sire presumed Plains Camp Male (her mating partner) - not confirmed.
nodes.fate: Moved to a new den after a week and not seen again; no suckle marks on 20 Nov 2025 - presumed lost.
nodes.notes: Group entry.

nodes.label: Birmingham male with the hanging dreadlock (most impressive male)
nodes.birthNote: Born ~2010.
nodes.fate: Unclear which of the last two Birmingham males he was; one fell to / fled the Ndzhenga Males in 2021-22.
nodes.notes: Repeatedly visited the Tsalala female; blog identifies "a Birmingham male" as the father of her cub (Dec 2019). Whether he is the same male who killed a Tsalala sub-adult in 2017 is not stated.

nodes.label: Last surviving Birmingham male
nodes.birthNote: Born ~2010 (coalition born 2010 per 2020-09-12).
nodes.fate: Pushed out by the Ndzhenga Males in Nov 2021-2022, fled to the western Sabi Sand, teamed with the Nkuhuma Male; referred to as "late" by Sept 2023. Cause/date of death not stated.
nodes.notes: Also called the "Birmingham Male" in 2022 posts.

nodes.label: Two Sparta lionesses born 2007 (cubs of the last Shaw's male)
nodes.birthNote: Born 2007 to the Sparta lionesses; sired by the Shaw's males' sole survivor.
nodes.fate: Still adult Sparta females in 2015; one killed in 2017 by the Ntsevu (Mhangeni breakaway) lionesses; Sparta pride down to one female by Nov 2020.
nodes.notes: Group entry.

nodes.label: Last surviving Shaw's male
nodes.birthNote: One of five males born in the late 1990s.
nodes.fate: Survived the Mapogo for 3 years; euthanised in poor condition in Mala Mala in January 2010.

nodes.label: Sparta cubs of 2016 (sired by the Matshipiri Males)
nodes.birthNote: Two Sparta lionesses each birthed two cubs in early 2016.
nodes.fate: One male cub killed by the Mantimahle coalition (mid-2017); others not accounted for.
nodes.notes: Group entry.

nodes.label: Ntsevu Pride original six lionesses (born 2013)
nodes.birthNote: Born 2013, daughters of the Mhangeni lionesses and the Majingilane Males (first batch of nine cubs, six of which became these lionesses).
nodes.fate: By 2023 two of the six had died (unknown circumstances); the rest are split between the Ntsevu and Kambula prides.
nodes.notes: Group entry. Named Ntsevu ("six" in Shangaan) in April 2017; Mala Mala calls them Kambula.

nodes.label: Mhangeni Pride second batch (12 cubs, 2015-16)
nodes.birthNote: Collectively 12 cubs (9 M + 3 F per 2018-09-29) born Oct 2015 - mid 2016 to the four Mhangeni lionesses.
nodes.fate: Pushed out by the end of 2017; fragmented; some died.
nodes.notes: Group entry; only included for the Majingilane lineage.

nodes.label: Ntsevu (Mhangeni breakaway) first cubs, 2016-17
nodes.birthNote: Early cubs of the Mhangeni breakaway lionesses; sire the Matimba (believed) and/or Matshipiri Males.
nodes.fate: No further sightings; none survived.
nodes.notes: Group entry.

nodes.label: Ntsevu cubs of 2018 - first Birmingham-sired litters that failed
nodes.birthNote: Litters of early 2018 (incl. 3 cubs found 2018-04-28 that vanished within a week).
nodes.fate: One litter killed by the very males that sired them (Birmingham) and another by a female within the pride (2018-09-09).
nodes.notes: Group entry.

nodes.label: Ntsevu cubs born 2018-19 sired by the Birmingham Males (the "12 subadults")
nodes.pride: Ntsevu Pride -> Ntsevu Breakaway Pride / Kambula Pride
nodes.birthNote: Born Aug 2018 - mid 2019 (6 males + 6 females per later posts; 13 cubs reported in Jan 2019; "presumably 15 cubs, 11 seen" in Nov 2019).
nodes.fate: After the Ndzhenga takeover (Nov 2021) the sub-adults fled; 4 females rejoined mothers by 2022; 2 males went to Kruger; 4 males + 1 female formed the Ntsevu Breakaway Pride.
nodes.notes: Group entry; counts vary between posts (see open_questions).

nodes.label: Ntsevu Young Males (Ntsevu Breakaway Males; later called Kambula Males)
nodes.birthNote: Six males of the 2018-19 Birmingham-sired cohort; later four males (3 b. 2018, 1 b. 2019).
nodes.fate: Two moved into Kruger; four roamed the SW with one sister; moved north in 2024 where they clashed with the Plains Camp Males; "Ntsevu Males ... back together" Jan 2025.
nodes.notes: Group entry. In Nov 2024 the "Kambula Males (Ntsevu breakaway Males)" are the Birmingham-sired males; in 2025-07 "Kambula sub-adult males" are a different, Ndzhenga-sired group.

nodes.label: Ntsevu cubs of April / October 2021 (Birmingham-sired)
nodes.birthNote: April 2021: litter of 5 (found 7 Apr 2021); Oct 2021: more litters; 11 cubs in total at Dec 2021-Mar 2022.
nodes.fate: 7 of 11 lost after the Ndzhenga arrival (Nov 2021); 4 survivors Mar 2022; 2 left by Aug 2022.
nodes.notes: 2022-04-11: 'last four cubs of the Birmingham Coalition'; 2022-08-03: youngest lost, another lost, 2 left. 2022-01-10 describes April-born cubs of 5 with only 3 left; dating of litters differs among posts.

nodes.label: Nkuhuma Male (Nkumati Coalition)
nodes.birthNote: Born ~2016 (2021-01-09: ~4 years old 'born 2016'; 7 years old in Sept 2023, 8 in 2024)
nodes.fate: Alive Jul 2026 (Nkumati Coalition, south-west Londolozi). Survived Ntsevu Breakaway attack (2023) and Plains Camp/Gijima encounters (2025).
nodes.notes: Left the Nkuhuma Pride and paired with the Styx young male (b.2016) by 2020-21; Styx partner 'mysteriously died'. Teamed in 2022 with the last Birmingham Male after Ndzhenga takeover; scarred right eyelid (2026-04-02), scar from altercation with his Birmingham father. Briefly paired with Skorro Male Jan 2024; formed coalition with the Talamati Male from mid/late 2024 ('together since mid-2024', 2026-02-12); named Nkumati (2026-02-09).

nodes.label: Othawa Male (also written Ottawa)
nodes.birthNote: Born early 2015 (2021-01-09: five year old Othawa male); 2018-09-17 says 3.5 yrs; 2019-12-02 inconsistently says 'about seven years old'.
nodes.fate: Died 2021. Posts say he was killed by the Birmingham Males after pushing too far east into their territory (2024-08-05, 2024-08-26); in Jun 2021 the Birmingham Males had 'triumphed over' him (2021-06-22); a deceased male is photographed by Sept 2021 (2021-09-20).
nodes.notes: Lone male, joined Mhangeni pride Dec 2019, mated with Ntsevu lioness Mar 2020 (2020-03-24). Dominant over south-west/west Londolozi. Contradictions: age in Dec 2019; cause of death (see fate).

nodes.label: Skorro (Breakaway) Young Male
nodes.birthNote: Sired by the Orpen Males, themselves sired by the Matimba Males.
nodes.fate: Alive 2024; mated with the Tsalala Female Nov 2023.
nodes.notes: Matimba-line grandson (stated).

nodes.label: Talamati young male who joined Mhangeni Breakaways (2016)
nodes.birthNote: Young male in 2016; one of three Talamati males 'pushed into independence' (2016-04-02) and separated from his brothers in a fight with the Charleston males.
nodes.fate: Travelled with the Mhangeni breakaway sub-adults Aug-Sept 2016; later fate not stated.
nodes.notes: 2016-08-20: 'the Matimba males (who are his fathers and the only reason he hasn't been driven off by them)'. Not clearly the same as the later Talamati young males (b.2019).

nodes.label: Nkuhuma lionesses "Ridge Nose" and "Amber Eyes"
nodes.birthNote: Born ~Dec 2012; sired by the Matimba Males.
nodes.fate: Killed in 2024, presumably by the Mhangeni Pride.
nodes.notes: Group entry.

nodes.label: Original Mhangeni lionesses (four founders)
nodes.birthNote: Born 2009 (2021-12-07, 2022-09-19, 2024-06-10); conflicting 'born in 2008, eleven years old' in 2019-12-02. Two female cubs each from the two Tsalala Sisters.
nodes.fate: Fate of the individuals not stated: 4 adults in 2015-16, 3 adults in 2018-19, two 'original' lionesses (15 yrs, one toothless) still alive Jun 2024; 2026-02-12 lists no 2009-born adult.

nodes.label: Styx Male (young, blonde)
nodes.birthNote: Born 2021 (2026-07-07) to a Styx Pride lioness and one of the Ndzhenga Males.
nodes.fate: Alive Sep 2026, nomadic.
nodes.notes: Pairs with the Ntsevu breakaway female Oct 2024-2026. Injured a Kambula male and killed a cub in Feb 2025; chased off by his father. Possible coalition partner for Nkuhuma Breakaway Male. The 2026-09-05 post 'The Styx Male: A Growing Presence' is not in the local corpus.

nodes.label: Tsalala Sisters (Tailed Female and New Tailless Female)
nodes.birthNote: Both born December 2002 on Ximpalapala Koppie to the Original Tailless Female, sired by the Marthly Males (2021-12-07).

nodes.label: Mhangeni lioness born 2018 (sired by Birmingham Males)

nodes.notes: Cubs of Nov 2025 presumed sired by Nkumati Coalition (2026-07-07: 'The Nkumati coalition, having sired offspring with the Mhangeni pride'; the 2026-02-12 text does not name the sire explicitly). Linked to the 2018 litter by inference only.

nodes.label: Mapogo Males
nodes.origin: Six males (three born 2000, three born 2002) from the Sparta Pride lineage (a Sparta lioness was their littermate; "Sparta pride birthed the infamous Mapogo").

nodes.status: Disbanded; last two known as Makhulu and Pretty Boy (2015 caption); displaced by the Majingilane 2010.
nodes.notes: Killed the Rocky Male (2007) and most 2006 Tsalala cubs; killed one Majingilane male in June 2010 before retreating west.

nodes.label: Majingilane Males
nodes.origin: Arrived in the Sabi Sand in 2010 as five males; one killed by the Mapogo in June 2010 (Legacy) - four thereafter.
nodes.territory: Most of Londolozi plus Mala Mala, eastern Singita and the northern sector - five prides - c.2010-2015; withdrew west from late 2014; Londolozi east/central lost to Matimba then Birmingham.
nodes.status: Entirely deceased by May 2018 (2018-05-07); three still seen Dec 2016, one seen Nov 2017.
nodes.notes: Three of the four stood off two Matimba males in Dec 2015. Their 8-year hold (2010-2018) is the benchmark the blog uses for later coalitions. Killed a 5-month-old Tsalala cub 26 Dec 2011 (Scar-Nose).

nodes.label: Ndzhenga Males
nodes.origin: Three brothers born 2015 in the N'waswitshaka Pride (Kruger NP, near Skukuza) plus an unrelated fourth male from the S79 Pride (KNP); joined as nomads around Skukuza; seen in Sabi Sand south from ~2020, trailing buffalo into Styx pride territory. nodes.label: Plains Camp Males
nodes.origin: Origin not stated. First described Sept 2021 as a young coalition (~5 yrs old, born ~2016) moving between Avoca and Birmingham territories; Apr 2021 post speculates unidentified young males might be 'Plains Camp Pride young males' (unconfirmed). Name derived from 'Plains Camp' area (not explained).
nodes.territory: Western sector of the Sabi Sand incl. western Londolozi (Sparta/Marthly), pushed east to the causeway/Plaque Rock (Jul-Aug 2024) and north into Nkuhuma territory (Jul 2024); by 2026 'moved further north following the Ximungwe/Bateleur Pride'.
nodes.status: Dominant in the west 2021-2026; by Jul 2026 under 'considerable pressure' on the Nkumati Coalition but still the largest coalition in the region.
nodes.notes: Took over the Mhangeni Pride after the Othawa Male's death (2021-22) (2022-09-19). Fought the Ndzhenga Males repeatedly (Aug 2024 chase; Dec 2024 standoff). Chased/attacked the Kruger + Southern Avoca Males (c.Nov-Dec 2024) and the Nkuhuma + Talamati Males (21 Jun 2025); a possible clash with the Gijima Males on the night of 15 Aug 2025 (one Gijima male had a facial gash and one Plains Camp Male limped on a back leg, 2025-08-17; the post does not explicitly name the opponents). nodes.label: Gijima Males
nodes.origin: Born in the Greater Kruger ecosystem ~2016-2017 (2026-07-07). Name 'Gijima' (Shangaan 'run') given by the southern properties due to their very unrelaxed nature on arrival in the Sabi Sand. Originally three males.
nodes.territory: South Sabi Sand -> from Aug 2025 central Londolozi (airstrip) and for the first time north of the Sand River (9 Nov 2025), exploring into Mala Mala; 2026-09: moving further north while Nwaswitshaka Males hold the south.
nodes.status: Dominant on Londolozi since Nov 2025, 'the dominant duo'; 2026-07-07 asks how much longer they have (~9-10 years old).
nodes.notes: Dominant over Styx, Southern and Msuthlu prides (2025-09-22) and took over the Kambula/Ntsevu prides in Nov 2025. Killed a Kambula sub-adult male (Nov 2025). Fought Nkuhuma + Talamati males (Aug 2025 airstrip) and Plains Camp Males (Aug 2025); blonde male beaten by Nkuhuma Breakaway Male in 2026. First reported on Londolozi in Jul 2023 (2023-07-30). Date discrepancy: 2026-04-04 says 'dominant in the Sabi Sands for six years'.

openQuestions.question: Founding story: Legacy (2021-12-07) says two Castleton females denned SEVEN cubs near Taylor's Crossing in 1998, of which the Original Tailless Female was the sole survivor; 2021-05-04 says the two founders denned FOUR cubs at Ximpalapala Koppie, one of which became the Original Tailless Female.
Date the Younger Sister lost her tail: 1 Nov 2011 (Legacy, Epic, 2018-03-22) vs 2012 (2016-05-23 'Tailless 2012').

Mother of the 2011 litters: not stated. Feb 2011 litter (3F+1M) assigned to the Tailed Sister and the May 2011 litter (3M+1F) to the Tailless Sister is INFERRED from 2016-03-31 ('older tailed female and her daughter from 2011'), 2018-03-22 and Legacy.
Birth year of the 2013 litter: winter 2013 (2019-03-07), 'late 2013' (2018-05-16), cubs 'circa Jan 2014', but Legacy tables and 2022-09-19 give 2014 ('older Tsalala Lioness (born in 2014)').

Fate of the three Tsalala Males (2013): Legacy says they dispersed to Kruger after Aug 2017 and were electrocuted at a giraffe carcass touching power lines; but they were seen on Londolozi in May and Aug 2018 (2018-05-16, 2018-08-21), and 2019-03-07 says only that they went south, 'as far as I know' into Kruger.

Who fathered the 2016-2017 Tsalala cubs: Matimba (2016 litters; Epic 'five youngsters') vs Majingilane possible (2018-05-07: 'can't be sure who the father actually was'); the 2017 breakaway cub is suspected Majingilane (2017-10-30). Also 2016-11-29 says a Matimba male mated with 'the tailless Tsalala lioness' although Epic says only the two non-breakaway females mated with the Matimbas.
Sex of the 2016 Tsalala cubs: Legacy gives all five as females; 2017-10-30 mentions a young male among the youngsters.

Birmingham coalition size over time: six originally (2020-03-02, 2021-06-22) vs five when first seen (2020-03-02, 2020-09-12, 2022-08-03); then 4 (2018), 3 (Aug 2019), 2 (Dec 2019). 2022-08-03 says one left north a few months after arrival and the rest were 'initial four ... then the three that remained'. 2020-03-02 (written 2018) says the fall from five to four followed a fight at a rhino carcass.

Birmingham reign dates: 2022-08-03 says dominant from late 2017; earlier posts show incursions in 2014-15 and 'five Birmingham males in the north' in Sept 2015; 2018 posts treat the Majingilane's departure (not a battle) as the opening.

Fate of the 'Birmingham male who died': 2019-08-15 says a male 'died' before helping sire the 2018-19 Ntsevu litters yet 2019-03-17 shows three Birmingham males; cause/date never stated. Last Birmingham male: fled west mid-2022 (2022-08-03) but 2022-11-10 says the coalition 'had dwindled down to one' and 2023-09-04 calls him 'late'.

Ntsevu litters/cub counts 2021: 2022-01-10 describes 11 cubs of mixed litters (5 born April 2021, 3 at 8 months, others 2-3 months) whereas 2022-04-11 says 'The Ntsevu Lionesses gave birth to 11 cubs in early October 2021'.
Number of Ntsevu cubs 2018-19: 'three cubs' (Apr 2018), '13 cubs' (Jan 2019), 'presumably 15 cubs, 11 seen' (Nov 2019), '12 cubs' / 'six males and six females' (2022-23).

'Her granddaughters': posts call the Ntsevu lionesses the granddaughters of the (new) Tailless Female (2018-05-30, Legacy) - they are the Tsalala Sisters' granddaughters via the Mhangeni lionesses, i.e. great-granddaughters of the Original Tailless Female and grand-nieces of the Tailless Sister.

Mhangeni Lioness b.2009 called the Tsalala Female's 'great aunt' (2022-09-19): by the stated pedigree she is an aunt (if daughter of the Tailed Sister) or first cousin once removed (if daughter of the Tailless Sister).
Cause of the Original Tailless Female's death (2013): Legacy states she was mauled by the Mhangeni females; 2018-05-30 and 2018-05-20 say 'suspected'. Epic does not state a cause.

Cause of the 2013 female's death (20 Nov 2021): bite marks on neck; Legacy says 'unsure of the exact details ... killed by other male lions'; 2023-12-11 says the Plains Camp Males are 'believed to be responsible'.

Number of cubs the Majingilane killed at the 2010 takeover: Legacy 4 (2 + 2) of the 2008-09 cohort; Epic 'four of the Tsalala cubs'. Majingilane arrival size: 5 (Legacy; 2019-08-15 '5-up') vs 'four' in other posts; 2015-12-14 shows 4 present in 2014.

Identity of the 'Kambula Males': 2024-11-11 and 2025-01-16 use 'Kambula/Ntsevu Males' for the Birmingham-sired Ntsevu breakaway males; 2025-07-14 uses 'Kambula sub-adult males' for 7 Ndzhenga-sired sub-adults.
Which Matimba male is 'dark-maned' vs 'hairy belly' vs 'ginger'/'blonder': blog uses all labels; mapping (dark-maned = hairy belly; ginger = lighter-maned = 'blonder') is inferred.

Tsalala Female 2019: 2024-05-28 says she mated with Plains Camp Males in Feb 2024 but 2024-02-19 says she mated with the Skorro Male in Nov 2023 and Plains Camp Males a month later (Dec 2023); sire of the 2024 cubs given as Plains Camp 'most certainly' but the Skorro male cannot be excluded.

Whether a litter exists in Feb 2026: 2026-02-08 follows 'signs' of a den at Ximpalapala Koppie but no cubs are seen; paternal candidates (Gijima Males, a large unidentified male at the koppie) not resolved.

Date of Mhangeni formation: 2010 (2016-04-18, 2016-09-07), 'late 2011-Jan 2012' (2021-12-07, final separation after the Jan 2012 flood), or named only when cubs arrived in 2013 (2016-09-03). Posts of 2024-06-10 say the Ntsevu 'broke away to form the Ntsevu Pride in 2015'; 2017-04-29 / 2017-11-06 say 2016-17.

Paternity of the 2013 Mhangeni cubs and the 2015-16 litter: stated as Majingilane (2018-02-27, 2018-11-08, 2016-05-10) - but 2017-01-09 says Mhangeni Breakaway cubs were believed sired by the Matimba males and 2017-04-29 says those litters failed. The 2024-06-10 post conflates 'offspring from this litter' (2013) with Ntsevu forming in 2015.

Mhangeni foundresses' birth year: 2009 (2021-12-07, 2022-09-19, 2024-06-10) vs 2008 (2019-12-02); '11 years old' in Dec 2019 implies 2008. Their sires are the Mapogo per 2021-12-07/2024-06-10 - but 2019-12-02 does not say.

Number of 2013 founders still alive: 6 original Ntsevu lionesses; 2 lost early/mid 2023 (2023-06-19, 2024-03-21), 3 in the Ntsevu faction (2024-03-21), 1 in the Kambula faction. 2023-07-19 says two mothers (4 cubs and 5 cubs) 'died', consistent with the loss but not proven to be the same two.

Kambula Pride composition: 2024-03-21 'last original lioness + five female offspring' (6 total) vs 2024-04-11 'five lionesses' vs 2025-01-21 'four females from the same litter' vs 2025-07-14 'five adult lionesses'. Likely 1 original + 4 daughters = 5, but unresolved.

Cub counts for the 2018 Birmingham-sired litters and sub-adults vary: 15 presumed (2018-11), 13 (2019-01), 11 + 4 (2019-11), 11 (2021-08, 5M/6F), 11 (2022-05, 5F/6M), 12 (6M/6F, 2022-08), 10 (2021-08), 12 with 8 males/3 females (2019-11). Sex ratios disagree.

Counts for the Ndzhenga-sired 2022-23 cohort: 21 cubs (2023-06-19), 24 (2023-07-19), 12 remain (Jul 2023), 13 (Apr 2024), 12 sub-adults 8M/4F (Feb 2025), 11 sub-adults 7M/4F (Jul and Nov 2025, even after a male was killed).
Sub-adult male killed by the Gijima Males (Nov 2025): the blog still lists 7 young males after the death in 2025-11-19, so either the kill happened before the 11 count or the count was not updated.

Ntsevu lioness thought infertile: 2020-08-18 says she may have given birth to two cubs; 2024-08-15 says she is barren and has 'never been able to fall pregnant'. Which of the six is the barren one is never stated.

Date of Ntsevu trio litter: 2023-12-17 says early August 2023 (first seen 23 Oct 2023) vs 2024-08-15 says 'November 2023' (1 male, 2 females). The 5-cub litter of 2021-04 vs 5 born 'in April this year' (2022-01-10) and 11 cubs born 'early October 2021' (2022-04-11) also differ in timing.

The 'last Birmingham cubs' (2021 litter): 2022-04 four survive; 2022-08 two survive; 2024-03 caption 'the 2 remaining youngsters'. Their sexes are never given; whether the pair belongs to the Ntsevu Pride proper is unclear.
Birmingham Males: 5 original (2022-08-03, 2019-08-15), 6 (2021-06-22), 4 in 2018, 3 in early 2019, 2 by Dec 2019, 1 by Nov 2021; date and cause of the death of the first male is not given.

Ndzhenga and Gijima: 2023-06-19 says the S79 Ndzhenga male was injured by the Gijima Males in April 2022; 2025-08-21 says the Ndzhenga 'killed the third Gijima Male' months after arriving; does that refer to a fight in late 2021/early 2022?

Msuthlu Pride origin: described as 'formerly the Talamati Breakaway Pride' (2025-10-05) and 'first met in 2022' (2026-04-04), yet 2026-04-04 says all 14 lions were sired by the Gijima Males. It is unclear whether the 2022 Talamati Pride sub-adult females (daughters of the Northern Avoca Males) are the Msuthlu adults.

Sire of the Styx Male: 2025-02-20 says one of the Ndzhenga Males is 'actually his father'; 2022-11-10 says Ndzhenga Males sired litters with the Styx Pride but Styx Male b. 2021 pre-dates their arrival at Londolozi (Nov 2021) - plausible only if they were consorting in 2020-21 as the posts suggest. His mother is never named.
Whether the Ntsevu Breakaway Female's mother is any specific lioness: 2024-10-02 says she is 'the daughter of the one female in the Pride', an unclear phrase, so no maternal link is asserted.

Othawa Male: age at 2019-12-02 ('about seven years old') conflicts with 2018-09-17 (3.5 years) and 2021-01-09 (born early 2015). Exact death date not given (between Jun 2021 and Nov 2021). Origin pride unknown.
Whether 'Othawa lionesses' (2018-05-07) are the same as the 'Othawa Pride' of 2026-02-12 is not stated.

Relationship of the Original Tailless Female and the Tailless/Tailed 'Tsalala Sisters' to other agent groups (Tsalala data) is only captured at the level needed to anchor the Mhangeni lineage; consult the Tsalala file for details.
The 'Southern Pride' lioness's cubs (b. ~Oct 2020) fate and the sire of those cubs are unstated; the 2025 'new offspring' are said to be protected by the Gijima Males.

SCOPE NOTE: Several items in the brief are leopards or cheetahs, not lions, and were not entered as lion data: Three Rivers Duo / Three Rivers Female / Three Rivers Young Male (leopards, 2023-07-09, 2025-01-19), Nkoveni Female and her cubs/'Nkoveni Trio'/'Nkoveni duo' (leopards; the 2024-11-17 'Kambula Pride ambush the Nkoveni Trio' post is a Nkoveni Young Female leopard killed by the Kambula lions), Xinkhova Female (leopard), Flat Rock Male (leopard, 2022-10-24), Ximungwe Female/Young Male (leopards). Only the lion 'Ximungwe Pride' (renamed Bateleur Pride) is recorded.

Formation date of the Mhangeni Pride is inconsistent: 2010 (Majingilane arrival, several posts), Jan 2012 (flood; 2021-12-07), 'newly-named Mhangeni pride' in Sept 2013 (2016-09-03), and 'formed in 2013' (2016-10-10). Name origin ('Meaning Aloe') only in 2021-12-07.

Birth year of the four Mhangeni founders: 2009 (2021-12-07, 2022-09-19, 2024-06-10) vs 2008 and 'eleven years old' (2019-12-02). Also whether they were daughters of the Tailless Female (2016-04-30 'Tailless female's daughters') or her granddaughters (2017-05-01/2021-12-07/2022-01-10).
Original Tailless Female's death (2013): 2021-12-07 states she was mauled by the Mhangeni females; 2018-05-20 says 'suspected'.
Fate of the two original (2009-born) Mhangeni lionesses: still alive Jun 2024 (aged 15; one toothless); the Feb 2026 pride composition lists no 2009-born adult. No death reported.

Mhangeni pride litter counts differ: 12 cubs 'between them' (Sept 2016) with 9M/3F (2018-09-29); 4 cubs of one lioness seen Sept 2018; cubs from Othawa Male counted as 2, then 3, then 'one 2021-born survivor'; Plains-Camp cubs 9 (2023), 10 (2024), 3 survivors (2026).
Paternity of the four Mhangeni cubs born Nov 2025 is implied (Nkumati Coalition) in 2026-02-12 and stated generally in 2026-07-07, but never explicit.

Othawa Male: age in Dec 2019 given as ~7 (2019-12-02) but he was born ~early 2015 (2018-09-17: 3.5 yrs, 2021-01-09: 5 yrs). Cause of death: killed by Birmingham Males (2024-08-05, 2024-08-26) vs 'recently triumphant over' (2021-06-22). Exact date of death 2021 unknown.

Plains Camp Males' origin (natal pride) is never stated; Apr 2021 post only speculates 'Plains Camp Pride young males'. Which Plains Camp male limped in Aug 2025 or is the 'smaller' male blamed for the Tsalala cubs is not specified for individuals.

Gijima Males: timeline conflict. 2023-06-19 says they injured a lone Ndzhenga male in April 2022; 2025-08-21 says the Ndzhenga Males killed a third Gijima male 'just months after' arriving (Nov 2021); 2026-04-04 says they have been dominant in the Sabi Sands for six years; first Londolozi sighting is Jul 2023. Only the 2025-08-21 post mentions a third Gijima male.
Ndzhenga Males in 2026: 2026-04-04 says they pushed north and are siring Nkuhuma cubs; 2026-07-07 says two Ndzhenga males 'from the south' ventured onto Londolozi.

Two different 'Styx Male' individuals: (a) Styx young male b.2016 who paired with the Nkuhuma Male and 'mysteriously died'; (b) Styx Male b.2021, son of an Ndzhenga male (alive 2026). Posts do not always distinguish them.
Nkuhuma Male's father: 'sired by the Birmingham Males, so either his son or nephew' (2022-08-10) vs 'his late father, the Birmingham Male' (2023-09-04). Which Birmingham male is unstated.

Matimba chronology: Matimba Males are credited with siring Nkuhuma lionesses born Dec 2012 (2024-07-31) and Talamati cubs from 2011, but the Matimba pair first appeared on Londolozi in Sept 2015 (2017-03-02) and were two of an original coalition of six from the Manyeleti; whether 2011-2012 siring is by the same males is unclear.

The Talamati young male seen with the Mhangeni breakaways in 2016 (Matimba-sired) is not linked to the later Talamati cohort (born 2019, Northern Avoca-sired). The Talamati Males (2) vs 'one of the Talamati Young Males' that died in 2024: cause/date not stated. 2022-07-25 calls Talamati 'the newest pride' although Talamati males were noted from 2016.

Msuthlu Pride: 2025-10-05 says it was 'formerly the Talamati Breakaway Pride'; 2026-04-04 says first encountered 2022 in the north, 4 adult females with 14 lions, sired by Gijima Males. How/when the Talamati Breakaway formed and whether its females are the four ~5-year-old Talamati lionesses of 2023 is not stated (speculation only).

Nkuhuma Breakaway male: described as '4 years old' in Aug 2025 (2025-08-04) and in Jul 2026 (2026-07-07) with birth year 2022; mother (Ridge Nose or Amber Eyes) and which of the pair raised the cubs not specified. The adult lionesses' death is dated only to 'recent months' before Jul 2024 and attributed 'presumably' to the Mhangeni Pride.

Northern Avoca Males: counts conflict (three brothers with two together and one apart in Sept 2020; 'coalition of two brothers' Jun 2021; one survivor by Dec 2022); the cause and dates of the brothers' deaths are not given; identity of the dark-maned male with the Talamati vs the single survivor in 2024.
Skorro Male (Skorro Young/Breakaway Male): mother and exact age unknown; no sighting after Feb 2024 in these posts. The unidentified large male at Ximpalapala Koppie on 2026-02-08 was not identified.
Fate of the Kruger + Southern Avoca coalition after Jan 2025: the Southern Avoca Male appears last as 'very weak' in the south (2025-01-16).

Cross-agent contradiction noted: 2021-12-07 says the three 2014 Tsalala young males were electrocuted in Kruger after dispersing in Aug 2017, but 2018 posts (2018-05-16, 2018-05-30) show the three males alive with the Tailless female in 2018. Tailless/Tailed Tsalala lioness deaths, Sparta, Ntsevu and Kambula details belong to other agents.

2016-11-29 says the Mhangeni Breakaway cubs (born late 2016) were 'not fathered by the Majingilane'; 2017-01-09 says the Matimba males are believed to be the fathers; 2017-03-02 and 2017-04-29 imply Matshipiri/Matimba matings; actual sire of the Ntsevu first litters is not confirmed.
Date discrepancy: the Ntsevu Breakaway Pride is said to have formed from the 2013 litter 'in 2015' (2024-06-10) but was renamed in April 2017 (2017-04-29).
